utility: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Bureau of Waterworks
grade_reason: Grade B. Every rate is now read from an instrument or a rate table of the publisher's own: the water charge from the ordinance that sets it, the sewerage charge from the Bureau's calculation-method table, and the waiver from the announcement that made it. The reading reconciles against the Bureau's own figures at eight volumes across water and sewerage, three of them on bills issued under the waiver. What holds it below Grade A is §2.5 and nothing else: the ordinance prices twelve bores and the tables three, and none of them designates one as the ordinary single dwelling. 20 mm is used because the Bureau's own residential worked example uses it, which is evidence and not a designation, and the 13 mm alternative is priced in the scope disclosures so a reader can see what the choice is worth.
statutory_basis: Tokyo Metropolitan Water Supply Ordinance (東京都給水条例), arts. 23, 23-2 and 23-3

continuity.note: The Bureau's own ready-reckoner, captured 18 August 2026, states on its face that it applies from the December 2019 billing month and publishes it as current. A revised table would appear at that address; the table is the supersession check. The ordinance capture carries the amendment history to Reiwa 7 and shows no change to arts. 23-2 or 23-3 since Heisei 16.

reference_connection.designation: Neither instrument designates an ordinary bore. 20 mm is taken because the Bureau's own residential worked example is computed at 呼び径20ミリ and reconciles exactly against the ready-reckoner at 59 m3. Under §2.5 that is documented suitability for an individual dwelling rather than a designation, so it is printed as scope. The strict smallest-priced tie-break would select 13 mm at ¥860 a month, which is priced in the scope disclosures.

billing_formula.evidence: Art. 23(1) of the ordinance states the multiplier and the truncation in terms. Previously this was inferred from a worked example; it is now read from the instrument.
billing_formula.rounding_period_note: The yen is dropped once, from the two-month total, not from each month. Six of the seven reconciliations cannot tell the difference; the app screen at 32 m3 can. Two months of 16 m3 under the waiver come to 1,756 yen of volumetric charge and 175.6 of tax, and the Bureau prints 1,931 — truncating each month first would give 1,930. At the scenario volume neither reading has a fraction to drop, so the published figure is unaffected; it is recorded because a rounding rule that happens not to bite is still a rounding rule, and the next volume may not be so accommodating.

basic_volume_note: The first 5 m3 a month is a basic volume INCLUDED IN THE BASIC CHARGE for bores of 25 mm and under, not a zero-rated first tier. The ordinance's volumetric table simply begins above 5 m3. Modelled as a zero-rate block because the arithmetic is identical, and flagged because the two are different claims — and because under the waiver the allowance survives while the charge it belongs to does not.

component_states.basis: Art. 23(1) sets the charge at 110/100 of the sum of the two components. The operative multiplier is in the ordinance, so the question of which statutory rate applies to a water supply does not have to be answered separately to compute the bill — the instrument that sets the charge states it.

Read from the Bureau's own sewerage rate table on the calculation-method page, which prints all nine bands and their effective date, and confirmed against the ready-reckoner at two volumes that fix both of the boundaries the scenario touches. It was previously read out of the ready-reckoner's sewerage column. The Bureau of Sewerage's own schedule is still not captured; this is the collecting utility publishing the rate, which is one remove from the levying authority and is not an inference.

Closed on 18 August 2026 by the announcement itself, dated 15 May 2026, with the Bureau's own guidance page beside it. The instrument gives every term §5.4 needed: four months of the Reiwa 8 summer, the 5–6 and 7–8 or the 6–7 and 8–9 billing months by meter-read cycle with the first waived reading on 1 June, the bores 13, 20 and 25 mm, no application required, and the basic charge of the water charge and nothing else. It also settles what the split rests on: the measure is funded by a transfer from the metropolitan general account and amends no charging article, so the structural price is not a reconstruction of a suspended tariff — it is the tariff, unchanged and still standing under the relief.
component_states.was_blocking: the payable price, which is the headline. The record could prove ¥140.80 per m3 and not the ¥55 a household actually paid.

component_states.question: §2.5 wants the bore the utility designates, or failing that the smallest documented as suitable for a single dwelling. Neither instrument designates one, and the ready-reckoner prices 13, 20 and 25 mm side by side.
component_states.resolution: Resolved as scope under §5.1. For a given bore the bill is exactly one number and U = 0; which bore the household has is a scope disclosure, as it is for Seoul and for London's metered account. It is printed, and the 13 mm figure is printed beside it.

components.name: Basic charge (基本料金), 20 mm
components.rate_display: ¥1,170/month at 20 mm; ¥860 at 13 mm; ¥1,460 at 25 mm. Includes the first 5 m3.

components.name: Volumetric charge (従量料金)
components.blocks_note: The four bands above 50 m3 were never read before the calculation-method page was captured; they are irrelevant to the R180 scenario and they are part of the tariff, so they are stored.

components.name: Consumption tax (消費税等相当額)
components.rate_display: 10%, set by art. 23(1) of the ordinance as a 110/100 multiplier

components.name: Sewerage basic charge (下水道基本料金)
Consumption tax on sewerage
components.rate_display: 10%, applied to the sewerage charge and truncated separately

temporary_policy_adjustments.amount_or_rule: basic charge waived in full for 13, 20 and 25 mm connections
temporary_policy_adjustments.period_note: Four months, billed as the 5–6 and 7–8 months for a property read in an odd month and the 6–7 and 8–9 months for one read in an even month, with the first waived reading taken on 1 June. Modelled as a single month. The payable price is period-dependent in a way one monthly figure cannot express.
temporary_policy_adjustments.funded_by: a transfer from the metropolitan general account. The Bureau states the measure therefore does not affect the water undertaking's financial management or its capital programme — which is the same fact, from the issuer's side, that keeps the underlying tariff unchanged.
temporary_policy_adjustments.issuer_characterisation: a temporary special measure limited to this summer
temporary_policy_adjustments.repetition_note: The same measure ran in the summer of 2025. A measure the issuer calls limited to this summer has now happened two years running. Recorded as the issuer states it, with the repetition noted.
temporary_policy_adjustments.application_note: 申請不要 — stated in the announcement. Nothing is means-tested and nothing is claimed, so this is a feature of the charge and not a Rule 3.1 elective reduction.
temporary_policy_adjustments.instrument_note: No ordinance was amended. The measure is announced by the Bureau under its own authority and paid for out of general revenue. That is why the structural price here is not a reconstruction of a suspended tariff: the tariff never went anywhere.

excluded.reason: The public bath-house rate under arts. 23-2(2) and 23-3(2) is a business category, not residential.
Rule 3.1: the ordinance's basic-charge exemptions for recipients of livelihood assistance and child-rearing allowances are status-tested, not a universal automatic feature of the tariff.
Rule 3.1: art. 30(4) reduces the charge for payment by account transfer. A payment-method discount is elective and not a feature of the tariff.

scope_disclosures: Reference account is a separately metered dwelling on a 20 mm connection in the 23 wards. At 13 mm the same household pays ¥1,771 a month for water — ¥118.07 per m3 against ¥140.80 — and the difference is entirely the basic charge.
Art. 23-4 allows the per-dwelling rates to be applied to flats in a shared-meter building on application, with the bore deemed 13 mm. That is a different reference customer.
Musashino City is inside Tokyo Metropolis and outside this jurisdiction.
Which four months of the waiver apply depends on the property's meter-read cycle.
Billing is bi-monthly. The monthly figure is the ordinance's own per-month computation, which is how the two-month table is built.
shape_note: A rising block tariff with a basic volume inside the fixed charge, so the per-cubic-metre price falls to about 15 m3 and then climbs. Tokyo is the only city in the Index whose payable and structural prices differ by a factor of more than two.

jurisdiction.note: City is a display layer. The observation belongs to jurisdiction x utility x service area x customer class x schedule x period.

cases.note: Basic charge 0 under the waiver; volumetric 2 × (22 × 5 + 128 × 10) = 2,780; tax 278. This is the payable price reconciled against a bill, which no other city in the Index can offer for a relief measure.

cases.note: 2 × (22 × 5 + 128 × 6) = 1,756 of volumetric and 175.6 of tax truncated to 175. The truncation rule is visible in a live bill rather than inferred from the formula.

public_reconciliation.limits: Every case above is a bi-monthly total, because that is how Tokyo bills. The monthly figure this record publishes is the ordinance's own per-month computation, which is the thing the two-month table is built from and is not itself printed by anyone.

water_supply.reason: Both prices are provable and both are published. Out of the base basket under §5.4 while the relief is live — not for any doubt about the figure, but because a basket of payable prices would move with a metropolitan press release and a basket of structural prices would silently drop a city that is charging half of them.

total_water_services.reason: The sewerage rate is read from the Bureau's own table and reconciled at four volumes, and the sewage volume is deemed equal to the metered water volume by the same page. Same §5.4 exclusion.

validation_note: Source verified, calculation verified, and reconciled against the publisher's own figures at seven volumes across water and sewerage — three of them on bills issued under the waiver, which reconciles the payable price and not only the structural one.
effective_from_note: The rate tables date themselves earlier than this record's effective_from: the water table applies from 1 January 2005 and the sewerage table from 1 June 1998. What moved in December 2019 was the tax multiplier, from 108/100 to 110/100, and the bill is the product of the two. effective_from is the date the charge as computed here took its present value; the underlying rates are older, and saying so is the difference between a tariff that was set in 2019 and one that has stood for twenty years.
sewage_volume_note: The volume of sewage discharged is deemed equal to the volume of water used (汚水排出量は、水道ご使用量と同量とみなして算出します). One metered volume therefore drives both streams, which is why a single scenario volume produces a total water services figure here without a second assumption.

waiver_scope.waived: the basic charge of the water charge, at 13, 20 and 25 mm
waiver_scope.evidence: The guidance page's FAQ asks whether the sewerage charge is waived and prints its answer collapsed, so the capture cannot read it. The specimen meter slip on the same page answers it in arithmetic instead: the water basic charge line reads ¥0 while the sewerage charge on the same slip is ¥4,136, which is 2 × 560 of sewerage basic charge plus 2 × (110 × 12) of volumetric plus ¥376 of tax, computed at full rates. A collapsed answer and a printed bill are not the same quality of evidence, and the printed bill is the better one.

verbatim_check_note: Four of the six captures behind this record are print-to-PDF, because the Bureau's site refuses automated fetching. Three of them store the PDF's own text layer beside the document, extracted mechanically: the kanji come out as mojibake and every rate in this record appears as digits, so the second pass reads the publisher's bytes rather than being told to skip them. The specimen bill figures are images inside the guidance page and are not in its text layer; they are reconciled instead, which is the stronger check.
